newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares shed 0.56 percent in correction.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares shed 0.56 percent in correction.

text.p: Shares in the Athens bourse ended 0.56 percent lower on Tuesday with all sectoral indices settling with mild losses. Market watchers said the slight correction did not change the market's bullish trend.
"The market corrected today following strong appreciation in recent sessions, but it remains on a clear bullish course," said Alexis Panagiotopoulos, a broker with Intersec.
Tuesday's drift did not fluster market participants with a strong belief in the market's upside potential.
"The index has formed a base just above 1,400, a level which will prove to be the starting point for a rally to around 1,600 after the Easter recess," he added.
Investors with a medium to long-term horizon were beefing up their long positions with blue-chip chased by both domestic and foreign investors, he said.

Greece's goal to join EMU by the year 2001 is an attainable goal but will require fast structural reform in the economy to establish sustainable convergence conditions, Bank of Greece governor Lucas Papademos told reporters on Tuesday.
The Athens share index finished 0.56 percent or 8.07 points lower at 1,432.97 from Monday's 1,441.04.
Turnover reached 15.5 billion drachmas on volume of 4.03 million shares.

Two 200,000-share blocks traded at 10,850 and 10,905 drachmas, rendered National Housing Bank the day's most active stock. Turnover in Alpha Credit was also substantial, including a 30,000 block traded at 19,700 drachmas.
Decliners led advancers 128 to 87 with 29 issues unchanged on 244 traded.
The fall was broadly based with all sector indices finishing lower. Banks gave up 0.53 percent and construction shares were off 0.89 percent.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted higher at 1,081.0-1,111.0. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, firmed 50 drachmas, to close at 6,150.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $61.68-$63.38. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The ING Baring Financial Products American- style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted lower at 2,244-2,440 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $13.08-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
